review_reference: Owner decision in chat by D-Eminence, 2026-11-02/03 (coordination notes, owner-decisions.md, Migrate item 7): "allowance 500 pages/facility/month (Textract+AI), only super admin raises, 100% pauses reading but not review/manual entry" (0110, Session B, Migrate AI reading); unsigned until the owner signs
evidence: 0110 (OCR page allowance, fair claim and AI usage), unsigned until the owner signs (reviewed_by is empty). Written on 0103; in the release it follows 0104-0109 but uses none of their objects and its preconditions ask for none of them. Backward compatible: three new tables and nine new functions in schema ocr, one more allowed transition in the existing trigger function ocr.validate_job_write (CREATE OR REPLACE; signature, SECURITY DEFINER, search_path, volatility, owner and ACL kept; md5 e9ea263ec9f29355eb9a6a81fd2d7b37 before, 58ff61a5b9b95685f6a6d3f938b8481f after), no other table, column, constraint, policy, trigger or function change (ocr.claim_worker_job keeps its body, checked again after), no row touched. Today's ocr-api, ocr-worker and identity-api images run unchanged. WHAT IT DOES. ocr.facility_page_limits (facility_id pk -> identity.facilities, pages_limit 1-100000, set_by_account_id, reason 1-240, set_at), ocr.page_usage (job_id pk; facility_id -> identity.facilities; usage_month = first day of the Africa/Lagos month of the first recording; pages 1-200; recorded_at) and ocr.ai_usage (primary key (job_id, attempt_no, model); model ^claude-[a-z0-9-]+$ at most 100 characters; facility_id -> identity.facilities; usage_month as page_usage; requests integer and input, output, cache read, cache write tokens bigint, all >= 0; recorded_at): no foreign key from either usage table to ocr.jobs, so the counts outlive the 24-hour working data and never block its deletion; row-level security forced, one policy for the OCR functions' owner, no grant to any runtime role, no patient or page text. Commands (SECURITY DEFINER, search_path pinned starting pg_catalog, ocr, owned by the owner of ocr.jobs): ocr.worker_page_allowance(uuid,uuid), ocr.record_worker_pages(uuid,uuid,integer,text), ocr.pause_worker_job_for_allowance(uuid,uuid,text), ocr.claim_worker_job_fair(text,integer,integer) and ocr.record_worker_ai_usage(uuid,uuid,text,integer,bigint,bigint,bigint,bigint,text) for hid_ocr_worker only; ocr.facility_page_allowance(uuid) and ocr.facility_ocr_usage(uuid,date) for hid_ocr_runtime (inherited by hid_ocr_api_runtime) and hid_identity_runtime (staff of that facility holding ocr.job.read via auth.membership_has_permission, or a platform session with platform.admin.access; the authorization is coalesced to false so a partial session is refused); ocr.set_facility_page_limit(uuid,integer,text) for hid_identity_runtime, platform_super_admin ONLY (coordinator decision: a cost decision; platform_admin, support admins and the facility read only), in a platform session with platform.admin.access, a correlation id and healthcare-operations; upsert; platform audit row admin.ocr.page-limit.set that 0064's rules accept; above use it makes the facility's parked queued jobs due now. The fair claim copies ocr.claim_worker_job's authorization, validation (plus a NULL lease and a cap outside 1-16 refused 22023), lease recovery and eligibility (the 0014 body as 0015 resolves its columns, written with #variable_conflict use_column as the rds-compat body; md5 b4e08bc13b9f0a38ed52c0e84f73ff6c checked after); it skips a facility with at least the cap of jobs processing under an unexpired lease (any provider), orders by that count, next_attempt_at, queued_at, id, FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED, and takes the candidate's facility with pg_try_advisory_xact_lock (never waits) and counts again after it, so the cap is exact among fair claimers; claims through the unchanged ocr.claim_worker_job take no such lock. ocr.record_worker_ai_usage: fail_worker_job's claim checks, model and counts checked (22023), one row per (job, current attempt, model) whose totals the call replaces, audit ocr.worker.ai_usage_recorded (attempt, model, counts) only when something changed. ocr.facility_ocr_usage: one row per model plus one row textract with the month's pages (tokens 0, always present), for the Lagos month containing the date (NULL this month). The trigger transition: a queued job whose last_error_code IS NOT DISTINCT FROM OCR_PAGE_ALLOWANCE_USED_UP (a NULL code never qualifies; with = it did, through three-valued logic, and the new suite case caught it) may move next_attempt_at earlier, not before now - 1 minute, with the next version and optionally a new correlation id, every other column unchanged. runtime-grants.sql's 0110 block makes exactly the grants the migration makes (USAGE on schema ocr to hid_ocr_worker, hid_ocr_runtime, hid_identity_runtime; the EXECUTE grants above; revokes from PUBLIC on the nine functions and three tables). PRECONDITIONS (catalog reads only; 55000 or 42501, nothing applied): ocr.jobs, identity.facilities, auth.accounts, audit.events present; none of 0110's objects (tables, the nine functions) and validate_job_write not already this file's body; md5 of ocr.validate_job_write, ocr.fail_worker_job, ocr.claim_worker_job (0014+0015 body or the rds-compat 0015 body), ocr.record_job_event, the six platform session helpers, auth.account_id_for_subject, auth.account_has_active_role, auth.account_has_platform_permission, auth.membership_has_permission, identity.has_active_membership, audit.authorize_platform_event; the trigger function's attributes; the two ocr.jobs triggers; 0064's three audit constraints and authority trigger; the four runtime roles where they exist (not superuser, not BYPASSRLS; on a fresh database the role bootstrap creates them after the migrations) and hid_ocr_api_runtime inheriting hid_ocr_runtime when both exist; the permissions ocr.job.read, platform.admin.access and the roles ocr_worker, platform_super_admin; one owner for ocr.jobs and the worker commands, which may create in schema ocr; the applier is it or a member that inherits it and may SET ROLE to it. POST-CHECKS: both bodies by md5, claim_worker_job still an accepted body, SECURITY DEFINER, search_path and owner of the eight commands, the shared reckoning SECURITY INVOKER, EXECUTE exactly as granted, the three tables' owner, forced row-level security, one policy and no other privilege, no foreign key from the usage tables to ocr.jobs. LOCKS: beyond ACCESS SHARE only the new tables, the session's temporary objects and SHARE ROW EXCLUSIVE on identity.facilities (three foreign keys); no index or constraint is added to ocr.jobs. PROVED on throwaway PostgreSQL 16 with pgvector (clusters created and deleted): fresh install 0001-0103 and 0110 (105 files) with the migrations before the role bootstrap, 0 pending after, role bootstrap and verification pass, all 78 database suites pass; upgrade of a 0103 database by the runner (plan 1 pending, dry run rolled back, apply, 0 pending; the file again answers '0110: already applied' and the runner applies nothing), the 0110 grants made by the migration equal those after a role bootstrap with this runtime-grants.sql (ACLs identical up to grantee order) and those of the fresh install; all 78 suites pass; the new suite fails on 0103. services/ehr-api/scripts/test-staging-schema-upgrade.mjs passed with a NOSUPERUSER NOBYPASSRLS migrator (MIGRATION_TARGET=rds, 104 baseline, 105 integrated; migration grants match runtime-grants.sql (2476); 185 row-security settings unchanged). Under a NOSUPERUSER NOBYPASSRLS owner (rds bodies) 0110 applies and the new suite passes in its non-bypass mode (157 cases; worker commands answer 55000 and the fair claim claims nothing, as every OCR worker command there). Negative copies stop with nothing applied: ocr.ai_usage, claim_worker_job_fair, facility_ocr_usage or record_worker_ai_usage already present ('already applied'), a changed ocr.claim_worker_job body (md5 mismatch). Concurrency: 12-16 concurrent fair claimers on two facilities with 30 and 10 queued jobs, 6 claims each with random hold times, end with exactly the cap processing per facility for caps 1, 2 and 3 (5 of 5 repeated runs at cap 2); the same harness with the advisory lock and recount removed ends with 4-8 per facility at cap 2. Mutants: 20 of 20 killed (trigger: = instead of IS NOT DISTINCT FROM, same time, no lower bound, attempt_count free; limit: platform_admin allowed; fair: no cap at all, no least-busy ordering, expired leases counted, only this provider counted, caps 0/17 accepted, no lease recovery; AI usage: no replace, no model check, replay audits, another worker's job; usage: AI month ignored, pages month ignored, no ocr.job.read, another facility, malformed rows); removing only the candidate-query cap or only the post-lock recount is not visible in one session (each layer alone holds the cap there) and the concurrency harness covers the recount. SUITE: services/ehr-api/test/database/ocr-page-allowance.integration.sql, 175 cases with a bypassing owner: security properties and grants of the nine functions, no table privilege for any runtime role, ai_usage keyed (job_id, attempt_no, model) with no foreign key to ocr.jobs, claim_worker_job unchanged; worker reads, recording, pause and resume as before; AI usage: two models for one attempt, totals replaced, replay writes no audit row, zero counts accepted, non-claude, capitalised, spaced, bare, NULL and 101-character models, negative or NULL counts, NULL or wrong token, another worker's job, a queued job, a staff subject, the OCR API and direct table reads refused; facility_ocr_usage this month (per model and textract 500), any day of the month, last month (a synthetic row only), next month (an empty textract row), clinic B last month (500 pages) and this month, refused for another facility or membership, no membership, a pharmacist, an inactive membership, no platform.admin.access, the worker, a NULL facility, P0002 for an unknown one; read by the super admin, a support admin and a platform_admin; limit refused for a platform_admin, a support admin, a non-admin, a facility session, no correlation id, another purpose and bad input; the trigger transition (coordinator condition) at clinic B: the allowance-parked job may move earlier to now, by a day with a new correlation id, or to 30 seconds ago, and is refused for 2 minutes ago, the same time, a later time, a cleared or changed error code, a changed summary, attempt_count, max_attempts, provider_job_reference or queued_at, and a skipped version (55000); queued jobs with no error code, WORKER_LEASE_EXPIRED and the near miss OCR_PAGE_ALLOWANCE are refused; the fair claim: bad caps (0, 17, NULL), leases (29, 3601) and providers refused, the least busy facility first although its job is younger, a facility at the cap skipped (a processing job of another provider counts, an expired lease does not), nothing when every facility is at the cap, ties by next_attempt_at, an expired lease of the provider recovered and reclaimed as attempt 2, lease, token and audit (cap and count before) checked.
